# Ciryl Gane Defeats Josh Hokit at UFC 334 to Retain Heavyweight Title

*The French champion secured his first title defense in New York against the former collegiate wrestling standout.*

**News** · 2026-11-16

Ciryl Gane completed the first successful defense of his UFC heavyweight championship on November 15, 2026, defeating American challenger Josh Hokit at UFC 334 in New York. The outcome was reported across sports outlets including Match TV, Sport-Express, and Championat, keeping the undisputed heavyweight belt in France.

## Heavyweight Defense in New York

The bout was staged as part of the UFC's November schedule in New York, a fixture on the promotion's calendar dating back to UFC 205 at Madison Square Garden in November 2016. According to Sportarena.kz and ВФокусе Mail, the contest marked Gane's first official defense since securing the undisputed division crown.

Facing Hokit, Gane turned back a challenger whose athletic foundation developed in collegiate wrestling. The victory extends Gane's tenure atop the division following several years competing in headline bouts across North America and Europe.

## Gane's Path to Championship Retention

Gane, who trains at the MMA Factory in Paris under head coach Fernand Lopez, transitioned to mixed martial arts following an undefeated professional Muay Thai career. The French heavyweight entered the UFC in August 2019, earning three consecutive finishes to open his promotional run.

At UFC 265 in August 2021, Gane won the interim UFC heavyweight championship in Houston, Texas, by defeating Derrick Lewis via third-round technical knockout. Gane previously contested undisputed championship bouts against Francis Ngannou at UFC 270 in January 2022 and Jon Jones at UFC 285 in March 2023, later rebounding with a second-round stoppage of Serghei Spivac in Paris in September 2023.

## Hokit's Background and Division Outlook

Hokit entered the championship clash at UFC 334 with a background from California State University, Fresno. Competing for the Fresno State Bulldogs, Hokit earned NCAA Division I All-American wrestling honors at 197 pounds in 2019 while also playing running back for the school's football team before focusing entirely on mixed martial arts.

Initial dispatches from Match TV and Meta MMA confirmed Gane's victory but did not specify the round or method of finish. With the championship retained in New York, Gane solidifies his standing as champion as the UFC prepares its heavyweight schedule for 2027.
